before: The STRING graph contained 1,242,422 direct train-test edge-index entries (9.06\% of all entries), corresponding to 621,211 unique undirected protein pairs. To assess connectivity sensitivity, we removed these direct edges and evaluated the resulting representations using the matched training protocol. Full FPP achieved mean AUC 0.7950 and AUPRC 0.6485, compared with 0.7702 and 0.6077 for edge-ablated FPP (Fig.~\ref{fig:connectivity}D; Supplementary Table 11). The paired ensemble AUC difference was +0.0248 (protein-clustered 95\% CI [+0.0066, +0.0494]; Supplementary Table 12). A separate partial edge-ablation sensitivity analysis examined different removal fractions and strategies (Fig.~\ref{fig:connectivity}E). This analysis used a separate training protocol and reused endpoint estimates, as detailed in Table~\ref{tab:run_sources} and Supplementary Table 8. Edge removal also changes graph normalization and retains indirect cross-partition paths, so the observed differences cannot be attributed exclusively to direct connections.
after: The STRING graph contained 1,242,422 direct train-test edge-index entries (9.06\% of all entries), corresponding to 621,211 unique undirected protein pairs. To assess connectivity sensitivity, we removed these direct edges and evaluated the resulting representations using the matched training protocol. Full FPP achieved mean AUC 0.7950 and AUPRC 0.6485, compared with 0.7694 and 0.6035 for edge-ablated FPP (Fig.~\ref{fig:connectivity}D; Supplementary Table 11). The paired ensemble AUC difference was +0.0264 (protein-clustered 95\% CI [+0.0078, +0.0521]; Supplementary Table 12). Partial edge-ablation comparisons used the same propagation operator and classifier settings at each removal fraction, with common endpoint fits across strategies (Fig.~\ref{fig:connectivity}E; Supplementary Tables 8 and 11B). Intermediate estimates varied across strategies and were not uniformly monotonic. Edge removal also changes graph normalization and retains indirect cross-partition paths, so the observed differences cannot be attributed exclusively to direct connections.
